Let’s start with the most important thing for remote work: the internet.

Right now, Telmex is the main (and pretty much the only) internet provider in San Carlos. They offer fast speeds and are generally reliable. Sometimes you’ll see brief outages, especially after bad weather, but overall it’s stable enough for Zoom meetings, video uploads, and everything else you might need for work.

If you want a backup or a more stable option, Starlink is available here too. You can buy the Starlink kit at Sam’s Club or STEREN Hardware Store in Guaymas, and it’s easy to set up. We’ve been seriously considering it ourselves since having a steady connection is essential for tech work.

Lately, I’ve seen Megacable company trucks installing cables around town, so it seems like more internet options might be coming soon, which is great news for everyone working online here.

Cafes with Free WiFi in San Carlos

If you like to work outside the house from time to time, San Carlos won’t disappoint. Almost every cafe or restaurant here has free WiFi and a relaxed vibe, so you can easily find a spot that fits your mood.

Here are a few of my favorite places to get work done.

Meri-Meri Coffee

Located right on the main boulevard, Meri-Meri is one of my go-to spots. It’s cozy, they have great pastries and coffee, and you can find plenty of outlets for your laptop. They also have a nice variety of bagels, croissants, and paninis—perfect for a working breakfast or lunch.

Cafe Buena Onda

The name means “good vibes,” and it really lives up to it. The staff is super friendly, the WiFi is reliable, and the food is delicious. It’s the kind of place where you can easily spend a few hours working without feeling rushed.

Turquesa Restaurant

Turquesa is more of a restaurant than a coffee shop, but it’s one of my favorite places for brunch when I want to work on something while enjoying a good meal. Their food is excellent, the coffee is strong, and the tables are big enough to spread out your stuff.

Everywhere Else

Honestly, most restaurants in San Carlos offer free WiFi and good food. Whether you’re at a seafood spot, or a local diner, you’ll find affordable meals and a comfortable atmosphere to get some work done.

Co-Working in San Carlos

There aren’t any official co-working spaces here yet, but you won’t really miss them. The cafes and restaurants have naturally taken on that role. You’ll see plenty of people working from their laptops while sipping coffee or enjoying breakfast.

If you prefer something quieter, many rental homes and condos in San Carlos are designed with remote workers in mind. You’ll find places with dedicated workspaces and reliable internet connections, which you can easily rent through Airbnb or through a certified realtor.

Final Thoughts

Working remotely from San Carlos gives you the best of both worlds. You can stay productive while enjoying the relaxed pace of a coastal town. Between Telmex, Starlink, and all the WiFi-friendly cafes, it’s easy to stay connected and get your work done without stress.

So whether you’re catching up on emails with a cappuccino in hand or taking a quick break to dip your feet in the ocean, San Carlos makes working remotely feel more like a lifestyle than a job.
